options: Splits a DataFrame into groups based on a column's values, so an aggregation can be applied to each group separately
Sorts a DataFrame alphabetically
Removes duplicate rows within each group
Merges two DataFrames together
questions.explain: groupby() organizes rows into groups sharing the same value in a chosen column, setting up an aggregation like sum() or mean() to be computed per group.

questions.q: In df.groupby("Region")["Revenue"].sum(), what does the result represent?
options: The total Revenue for each unique Region, with all matching rows added together
The Revenue of only the first row in each Region
A single grand total combining every region
The count of rows in each Region, not their Revenue
questions.explain: Every row sharing the same Region value has its Revenue summed together into one total per region.

questions.q: What is the Power BI equivalent of df.groupby("Region")["Revenue"].sum()?
options: A matrix visual with Region in rows and Revenue in values
A slicer filtering by Region
A calculated column
There is no equivalent concept in Power BI
questions.explain: Both achieve the same conceptual result — collapsing many rows into one summarized value per group — just through a visual instead of code.

questions.q: What does .agg(["sum", "mean", "count"]) do compared to calling .sum(), .mean(), and .count() separately?
options: Computes all three aggregations together in one line and one pass over the data, rather than three separate groupby calls
Only computes the sum and ignores mean and count
Is functionally identical to calling .sum() alone
Requires the DataFrame to have exactly three columns
questions.explain: agg() lets you request multiple aggregations from a single groupby call, producing a side-by-side comparison table in one line.

questions.q: Why might you choose .mean() over .sum() for a groupby aggregation?
options: When the question is about the typical/average value per group, rather than the group's total
.mean() and .sum() always return identical results
.mean() is required whenever grouping by a text column
.sum() can only be used with numeric columns, unlike .mean()
questions.explain: The choice of aggregation depends on the actual question — sum answers 'what's the total,' while mean answers 'what's typical' — both are valid depending on what you're trying to learn.
